chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who made a mistake in prayer and did not know whether he had prostrated once or twice. He said: 'He prostrates once more, and after the completion of the prayer, he is not required to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdat al-fara'ig).'

key_terms.سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ: The two prostrations of forgetfulness performed after the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one is unsure if they prostrated once or twice during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the specific ruling for *shakk* (doubt) regarding the number of prostrations, distinguishing it from general forgetfulness (*nisyan*) by exempting the worshipper from the post-prayer *sajdat al-fara'ig*. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that uncertainty in the structure of prayer is resolved by performing an extra prostration during the prayer itself, thereby validating the act without requiring additional compensation after the salam. This highlights the precision in Shia fiqh regarding the internal mechanics of prayer validity versus completeness.
